title: Renewal & expansion check-in - BlueHarbor Bank
summary: Quarterly renewal/expansion check-in. BlueHarbor is evaluating a capacity upgrade (additional dedicated GPUs), adding EU region routing for latency/residency, and a 12-month contract extension. Agreed to run a 72-hour benchmark on dedicated capacity and to send formal pricing and contract amendment. Security questions around SOC 2 and KMS were discussed; Redwood to share SOC2 report and KMS integration notes.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-14
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Evan Cruz (Redwood CSM); Alex Morgan (BlueHarbor), Sofia Ruiz (BlueHarbor), Diego Park (BlueHarbor), Maya Chen (BlueHarbor)

Summary: quick renewal/expansion checkin — focused on capacity upgrades and adding EU region for residency. agree to benchmarks and contract amendment.

00:00 Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you all making time today, I'll kick off — this is Jordan and with me is Priya our solutions engineer and Evan from customer success, we wanted to run through where you're at on the renewal and the expansion asks.
00:18 Alex Morgan: thanks Jordan, yeah we have our Q2 finance review coming up and we want to lock in capacity and timeline — main asks: more dedicated capacity for our peak processing windows, and ability to route traffic to eu-west for some european customers for data residency and latency.
00:34 Priya Nair: great, can you give a quick sense of current utilization and target headroom? like number of concurrent sessions or tokens per minute?
00:45 Diego Park: sure, right now on hosted we're seeing spikes up to about 2.5k rps of small gen calls during peak — that's approx 120k tokens/minute; our current reserved pool covers about 60% of peak, we want to target 90-100% to avoid throttles during promos.
01:05 Sofia Ruiz: and cost is a consideration — we were hoping dedicated pricing + some burst buffer would make sense; also curious about EU region pricing and whether that requires a separate reserved commit.
01:16 Jordan Lee: yeah good questions — we can do a dedicated GPU pool addition and configure autoscale/burst policies; pricing can be structured as a top-level reserved commit plus smaller burst. for EU region we typically provision a separate dedicated pool in that region which can be added to the contract as an add-on, so we'll include EU pricing in the sheet.
01:36 Maya Chen: on security, we need to confirm SOC 2 coverage, KMS/HSM options, and audit log retention for regulatory. also interested in explicit data path for eu routing.
01:48 Evan Cruz: totally, we'll share the SOC 2 Type II and the KMS integration docs — for EU routing we can show routing policies and the private deployment options, note that private on-prem would be a bigger lift but VPC with regional dedicated clusters is common.
02:03 Priya Nair: if we move to dedicated in eu-west, there are perf implications (kernel selection, sequence length, quantization) — we'll want to run a benchmark using your sample traffic to validate latency and cost. suggested acceptance criteria would be p95 latency under X, cost per 1k tokens no more than Y relative to hosted.
02:24 Diego Park: yes, we'll provide a representative traffic profile — mostly short prompts but occasional long-context ops analysis jobs. also KV cache stuff matters for latency— we saw some cache thrash on our test harness last quarter.
02:38 Priya Nair: thanks, we'll include KV/prefix cache settings in the test plan. for the benchmark we recommend a 72-hour run during a low-production window so we can capture autoscaling behavior.
02:51 Jordan Lee: quick question on timeline, Sofia — are you aiming to finalize by end of March to hit your fiscal quarter?
03:01 Sofia Ruiz: ideally yes, we want to have the contract amendment signed and capacity provisioned by mid-April. approval path: procurement + security sign-off, then finance.
03:12 Alex Morgan: also a note on fallbacks — if capacity is constrained, we may want Redwood to automatically route to a slightly lower-cost variant or to a hosted-tier fallback, what's the behavior today?
03:25 Priya Nair: we support smart routing policies — you can configure fallback to compatible model variants or regions, and set policy by latency or cost. we'll document best-practices for critical routes.
03:36 Diego Park: are there any limits on cross-region KV cache coherence or prefix sharing? That affected our multi-region setup before.
03:47 Priya Nair: current design keeps KV cache local to serving pool; cross-region prefix cache isn't synchronous — recommended approach is either pre-warm caches in the region or route traffic consistently to the same region for session affinity. we'll note tradeoffs.
04:05 Maya Chen: on encryption, does Redwood support customer-managed keys in KMS/HSM for both hosted and dedicated?
04:12 Evan Cruz: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we have an option for CMEK on enterprise plans, we'll share the integration docs.
04:22 Alex Morgan: perfect. about benchmarks — can Redwood provide the test harness or do we need to ship samples?
04:29 Priya Nair: Redwood will provide the harness and the test vectors; Diego will supply the traffic profile and a subset of sample prompts; we'll run it in your dedicated pool and provide the results and cost breakdown.
04:42 Jordan Lee: ok action items: I'll send pricing and contract amendment, Priya will set up the benchmark and Evan will share SOC2/KMS docs. any other questions?
04:51 Sofia Ruiz: just to confirm, if we extend 12 months do we get a committed discount band?
05:00 Jordan Lee: yes typical pricing includes step-down for 12-month commit and larger reserved volumes; I'll include tiers in the sheet.
05:09 Alex Morgan: and lastly, what about support SLA for dedicated — do we get faster ops response?
05:16 Evan Cruz: dedicated includes elevated SLAs and a 24x7 escalation path for capacity incidents; we can include that language in the amendment.
05:26 Jordan Lee: great, we'll follow up with the next items. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
